newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Anadarko's Algerian potential high - MEES.
newsitem.headline: Anadarko's Algerian potential high - MEES.

text.p: Oil output capacity at Algerian oilfields operated by U.S. firm Anadarko Petroleum Corp could be significantly higher than the firm's own estinates, the Middle East Economic Survey (MEES) reported on Monday.

Based on a study by Goldman Sachs U.S. Research, capacity at Anadarko's three Algerian fields is expected to reach 495,000 barrels per day (bpd) after the end of the decade, compared to the U.S. firm's forecast of 300,000 bpd, MEES reported.
If realised, the higher capacity would be a major lift in OPEC-member Algeria's attempt to raise its oil potential.
Algiers aims to lift crude output capacity to one million barrels per day (bpd) by 1999 from a planned 850-900,000 bpd this year with new deposits developed by foreign firms.
It has also targeted a capacity of between 1.1-1.2 million bpd by the year 2000.

Anadarko's production profile would be 180,000 bpd from the Hassi Berkine South (HBNS) field, 75,000 bpd from Hassi Berkine (HBN) field and 240,000 bpd from Qubba while the company's net reserves from its various interests in Algeria total 472 million barrels, Cyprus-based MEES reported.
HBNS output is scheduled to start in April with first-phase capacity of 60,000 bpd with peak rate of 180,000 bpd.
HBN, which will be jointly developed with Italian Agip's Hassi Berkine North (HBNN) concession, could be onstream in 1999 with a capacity of 75,000 bpd, MEES reported.
"Qubba is now considered the most significant discovery in Algeria during this decade and peak output may reach 240,000 bpd according to Goldman Sachs," MEES reported.
Qubba's straddles exploration blocks run by Anadarko (BKE field), Spanish CEPSA (ORD field) and Louisiana Land and Exploration Company (MLNE field).
Estimated gross reserves are approximately 1.2 billion barrels with a recovery factor at the high level of 50 percent using both primary and secondary programs, MEES said.
Algeria has an OPEC quota of 750,000 bpd though output has been running at 850,000 bpd, according to independent assessments.
Oil and gas dominate Algeria's economy with the oil and gas exports bringing in $12.6 billion in 1996. SS
